finding.claim: The purge handler calls checkPerm(u, "admin") but discards the boolean result, so the admin check is never enforced. Any caller who can reach the route runs purgeAll(). The sibling handler rotateKeys uses mustPerm and returns on failure; purge lacks that.
finding.source: Any authenticated (or otherwise reachable) HTTP user hitting the purge route. userFrom(r) at handlers.go:25 returns a user without the admin permission.
finding.sink: purgeAll() at handlers.go:27, a destructive admin-only operation.

trace.note: u := userFrom(r) takes the user from the request context
checkPerm(u, "admin") returns false for a non-admin, but the result is ignored and there is no return or error response

finding.guards_checked: checkPerm at line 26 is the only control and its return value is discarded. mustPerm (lines 16-22) would enforce it but is not used here. rotateKeys (lines 31-38) correctly uses mustPerm and aborts on failure, so it is SAFE. I only had handlers.go: no route table or auth middleware is present, so I could not check whether upstream middleware restricts purge. Any such middleware would have to check admin itself, because this handler does not.

verdict.guard_found: checkPerm at handlers.go:26 (returns bool, result discarded as a bare statement); mustPerm (16-22) is not used in purge. No route table or middleware exists in the directory (handlers.go is the only file).
verdict.reason: handlers.go:26 calls checkPerm(u,"admin") as a bare statement, discarding the bool, so purgeAll() at handlers.go:27 runs for any user who reaches the route, unlike rotateKeys at handlers.go:33-35, which returns on failure.
